intro.summary: Create a window, clear its back buffer with Vulkan, and present your first frame.
overview.heading: When to use Vulkan
overview.purpose: Vulkan is a cross-platform API for graphics and GPU compute. It suits engines and complex scenes that need control over memory, command queues, and execution order.
overview.choice: Choose Vulkan if you need low-level control across platforms such as Windows and Linux. It gives you a similar level of control to Direct3D 12 and requires more setup and synchronization code than OpenGL or Direct3D 11.
requirements.heading: 1. Set up the project
requirements.folder: In the LIMEN source directory, create a folder named first-vulkan. Save the next section's code as Main.hx inside it.
requirements.paragraph: Follow the LIMEN installation guide and copy limen.hdll and vulkan.limen into the app directory. You need a Vulkan driver that supports dynamic rendering, synchronization2, and timeline semaphores. Use source files and native modules from the same LIMEN version.
program.heading: 2. Render your first frame
program.intro: Acquire a swapchain image, record the clear command, and present the frame. The event loop then keeps the window open.
run.heading: 3. Build, run, and experiment
run.runtime: Run the commands from the directory containing Main.hx. If you use the bundled Windows runtime, copy hl.exe and libhl.dll from the build output into that directory and run .\hl.exe main.hl.
run.result: A window with a blue background should open. Close it, change the color or title in Main.hx, and run both commands again.
